shortlist.rationale: The Svitzer contract is firm (a signed contract to build four tugs), and it opens a new product and a new customer, so it is not routine. The press release gives no value, so size is estimated from quantity: 4 tugs x an assumed INR 50 crore (a low floor) = INR 200 crore, or 70.9% of TTM revenue of INR 282 crore. The company is loss-making (TTM PAT INR -226 crore), but no default, going-concern doubt or insolvency is in the packet and the order is itself the path to absorb fixed costs, so no disqualifier is applied; confidence is LOW because the value is estimated.

result.mechanism: Newbuild shipbuilding orders at a yard that had almost no revenue a year earlier: six 18,000 DWT IMO Type II chemical tankers for Rederiet Stenersen AS (USD 227 million, about INR 2,080 crore, signed 23 Jan 2026, after a Nov 2025 LoI), plus four 92,500 DWT ammonia dual-fuel bulk carriers for Energy ONE Limited (Category 4 band, INR 1,501-3,000 crore, 7 Apr 2026) and a Government of Oman training-ship export order (5 Feb 2026, value not stated). Management describes these as India's first of their kind.
result.rationale: 14-day freshness filter: the basis order was first announced 2026-01-23, more than 14 days before week 2026-05-25; Haiku had DEEP_RESEARCH. Size: the stated Stenersen contract (USD 227 million, about INR 2,080 crore, multi-year) is 737% of TTM revenue of INR 282.14 crore; delivery years not stated, so the annual effect is smaller. Firmness: the Stenersen and Energy ONE contracts are signed orders (Reg 30 'received new order'), so firm. Not routine: FY25 revenue was about INR 7 crore, and these are India's first chemical-tanker and ammonia dual-fuel orders, a step-change with new revenue streams. Losses are heavy (TTM OPM -110%) and the company exited CIRP this year, so stress is a real risk, but the orders are the operating fix and debt is not shown as high in the packet, so no disqualifier is applied; deep research must test funding and delivery execution.
result.what_changed: Revenue went from about INR 7 crore (FY25) to INR 282 crore TTM (FY26) and the company now reports a multi-year newbuild book; the company states a total order book of about USD 500 million. Delivery and revenue-recognition timing are not in the packet.
contradictions: Company's adjusted PAT of INR 34.5 crore (FY26, excluding exceptional loss on sale of legacy OSVs) vs reported TTM PAT of INR -225.9 crore in the packet
Company's total income of about INR 440 crore (incl. other income) vs packet TTM revenue of INR 282.1 crore
Company states the CIRP resolution plan was concluded with prepayment of CoC obligations, while the packet shows loss-making results (TTM OPM -109.8%)
